title: Melvin Van Peebles
shortDescription: Independent filmmaker whose Sweet Sweetback's Baadasssss Song ignited the movement
biography: Writer-director-star-composer whose self-financed Sweet Sweetback's Baadasssss Song (1971) proved a Black-led film could be a major independent hit, catalyzing the blaxploitation wave. A polymath who also worked in music and theater.

title: Gordon Parks
shortDescription: Photographer and director of Shaft (1971)
biography: Pioneering photographer, writer, and composer who became a landmark Hollywood director. His Shaft (1971) for MGM was the commercial breakthrough that made the studios embrace the genre.

title: Gordon Parks Jr.
shortDescription: Director of Super Fly (1972)
biography: Son of Gordon Parks, he directed Super Fly (1972), one of the genre's defining and most controversial films, before his early death in a 1979 plane crash.

title: Jack Hill
shortDescription: Director of Pam Grier vehicles Coffy and Foxy Brown
biography: Exploitation-cinema director and writer who shaped the genre's action-heroine template through Coffy (1973) and Foxy Brown (1974), both starring Pam Grier for American International Pictures.

title: Larry Cohen
shortDescription: Writer-director of Black Caesar and Hell Up in Harlem
biography: Prolific writer-director who brought a gangster-saga sensibility to the genre with Black Caesar (1973) starring Fred Williamson, scored by James Brown.

title: Ossie Davis
shortDescription: Actor-director of the proto-blaxploitation Cotton Comes to Harlem
biography: Acclaimed actor, playwright, and activist whose Cotton Comes to Harlem (1970) is widely cited as a key precursor that demonstrated the commercial appeal of Black-led crime comedy.

title: William Crain
shortDescription: Director of Blacula (1972)
biography: Television and film director who helmed Blacula (1972), the genre's signature entry into horror, for American International Pictures.

title: Jack Starrett
shortDescription: Director of Cleopatra Jones (1973)
biography: Actor-turned-director who made Cleopatra Jones (1973), pairing a glamorous action heroine with a big-studio release from Warner Bros.

title: Ivan Dixon
shortDescription: Actor-director of Trouble Man and The Spook Who Sat by the Door
biography: Actor and director who directed Trouble Man (1972), whose Marvin Gaye score became a landmark, and the politically charged The Spook Who Sat by the Door (1973).

title: Michael Campus
shortDescription: Director of The Mack (1973)
biography: Director of The Mack (1973), a defining pimp-and-hustler drama shot in Oakland that became one of the genre's most culturally durable films.

title: Richard Roundtree
shortDescription: Actor who played John Shaft; 'the first Black action hero'
biography: Former model who became an icon as private detective John Shaft in Shaft (1971) and its sequels, establishing the template for the genre's cool, self-possessed leading man.

title: Pam Grier
shortDescription: Foremost action heroine of the genre; star of Coffy and Foxy Brown
biography: The genre's definitive female star, whose tough, avenging heroines in Coffy (1973) and Foxy Brown (1974) made her a lasting cultural icon later celebrated in Tarantino's Jackie Brown.

title: Ron O'Neal
shortDescription: Actor who played Priest in Super Fly
biography: Classically trained actor who played the cocaine dealer Youngblood Priest in Super Fly (1972), one of the genre's most iconic and debated protagonists.

title: Fred Williamson
shortDescription: Former NFL star turned action lead (Black Caesar, Hammer)
biography: Ex-professional-football player nicknamed 'The Hammer' who became a leading man and later producer-director, starring in Black Caesar (1973), Hammer (1972), and Three the Hard Way (1974).

title: Jim Brown
shortDescription: NFL Hall of Famer turned action star (Slaughter, Three the Hard Way)
biography: One of the greatest football players in history who transitioned to acting, becoming an early Black action lead in films such as Slaughter (1972) and Three the Hard Way (1974).

title: Tamara Dobson
shortDescription: Model-actress who played Cleopatra Jones
biography: Fashion model who starred as the government agent Cleopatra Jones (1973), a rare studio-backed action heroine standing alongside Pam Grier as a genre icon.

title: Rudy Ray Moore
shortDescription: Comedian who created Dolemite
biography: Raunchy stand-up comedian and 'Godfather of Rap' who self-produced and starred in Dolemite (1975), a self-financed cult landmark of the genre's independent wing.

title: Yaphet Kotto
shortDescription: Actor in Across 110th Street and the Bond film Live and Let Die
biography: Versatile character actor who appeared in Across 110th Street (1972) and later crossed into mainstream cinema; a respected dramatic presence in and beyond the genre.

title: Jim Kelly
shortDescription: Martial artist and actor (Enter the Dragon, Three the Hard Way)
biography: Karate champion who became a martial-arts action star, appearing in Enter the Dragon (1973) and headlining Black Belt Jones (1974) and Three the Hard Way (1974).

title: Max Julien
shortDescription: Actor who played Goldie in The Mack
biography: Actor and writer who starred as the pimp Goldie in The Mack (1973) and wrote Cleopatra Jones, a key creative figure of the era.

title: Isaac Hayes
shortDescription: Composer of the Oscar-winning Theme from Shaft
biography: Stax Records soul auteur whose score for Shaft (1971) won the Academy Award for Best Original Song, proving the commercial power of the genre's funk soundtracks. He later starred in Truck Turner (1974).

title: Curtis Mayfield
shortDescription: Composer of the Super Fly soundtrack
biography: Soul and funk innovator whose Super Fly (1972) soundtrack, with its critical lyrics about drug culture, became more celebrated than the film and a landmark socially conscious album.

title: James Brown
shortDescription: 'Godfather of Soul'; composer of the Black Caesar score
biography: The Godfather of Soul, whose funk fundamentally shaped the era's sound; he composed the soundtracks for Black Caesar (1973) and Slaughter's Big Rip-Off (1973).

title: Marvin Gaye
shortDescription: Motown star; composer of the Trouble Man score
biography: Motown singer-songwriter whose only film score, Trouble Man (1972), stands as one of the genre's most acclaimed soundtracks.

title: Bobby Womack
shortDescription: Soul musician; composer of the Across 110th Street title theme
biography: Soul singer-guitarist whose title song and score for Across 110th Street (1972) became an enduring standard, later revived in Jackie Brown and American Gangster.

title: Roy Ayers
shortDescription: Vibraphonist and funk musician; composer of the Coffy score
biography: Jazz-funk vibraphonist and bandleader who composed the soundtrack for Coffy (1973), a key entry in the genre's musical canon.

title: American International Pictures
shortDescription: Low-budget studio that produced many genre staples
description: Independent studio specializing in low-budget genre films; the most prolific producer-distributor of blaxploitation, releasing Coffy, Foxy Brown, Blacula, Black Caesar, and Truck Turner.

title: Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer
shortDescription: Major studio that released Shaft
description: Major Hollywood studio whose distribution of the hit Shaft (1971) is often credited with reviving its finances and signaling that major studios would invest in the genre.

title: Warner Bros.
shortDescription: Major studio behind Super Fly and Cleopatra Jones
description: Major studio that distributed genre hits including Super Fly (1972) and Cleopatra Jones (1973).

title: Cotton Comes to Harlem
shortDescription: 1970 crime comedy widely seen as a genre precursor
description: Ossie Davis's 1970 adaptation of Chester Himes's novel; a commercially successful Black-led crime comedy often cited as the immediate precursor to the blaxploitation wave.

title: Sweet Sweetback's Baadasssss Song
shortDescription: 1971 independent film that ignited the movement
description: Melvin Van Peebles's self-financed 1971 film about a fugitive evading police; a surprise independent hit whose success is widely credited with launching blaxploitation.

title: Shaft
shortDescription: 1971 detective film; commercial breakthrough of the genre
description: Gordon Parks's 1971 film about private detective John Shaft; a major studio hit for MGM whose success mainstreamed the genre. Isaac Hayes's theme won an Academy Award.

title: Super Fly
shortDescription: 1972 film about a cocaine dealer seeking one last score
description: Gordon Parks Jr.'s 1972 film starring Ron O'Neal as the dealer Priest; a huge hit and a lightning rod in debates over the genre's glamorization of drugs, elevated by Curtis Mayfield's soundtrack.

title: Blacula
shortDescription: 1972 horror film; the genre's vampire entry
description: William Crain's 1972 horror film starring William Marshall as an African prince cursed to vampirism; a commercial success for AIP that spawned a sequel.

title: Trouble Man
shortDescription: 1972 crime film with a landmark Marvin Gaye score
description: Ivan Dixon's 1972 film about a slick private fixer, best remembered today for Marvin Gaye's acclaimed soundtrack.

title: Across 110th Street
shortDescription: 1972 gritty crime drama with a Bobby Womack title theme
description: Barry Shear's 1972 crime drama set in Harlem, noted for its gritty realism and Bobby Womack's enduring title song.

title: Black Caesar
shortDescription: 1973 gangster film scored by James Brown
description: Larry Cohen's 1973 rise-and-fall gangster saga starring Fred Williamson, with a soundtrack by James Brown, produced and released by AIP.

title: Coffy
shortDescription: 1973 revenge film that made Pam Grier a star
description: Jack Hill's 1973 revenge thriller starring Pam Grier as a nurse avenging her sister; an AIP hit with a Roy Ayers score that established the genre's action-heroine archetype.

title: Cleopatra Jones
shortDescription: 1973 action film with a glamorous government-agent heroine
description: Jack Starrett's 1973 Warner Bros. action film starring Tamara Dobson as a globe-trotting government agent battling drug traffickers.

title: The Mack
shortDescription: 1973 Oakland-set drama about a pimp's rise
description: Michael Campus's 1973 drama starring Max Julien as the pimp Goldie, with Richard Pryor; shot in Oakland and among the era's most culturally influential films.

title: Foxy Brown
shortDescription: 1974 revenge film starring Pam Grier
description: Jack Hill's 1974 AIP revenge thriller starring Pam Grier, originally conceived as a Coffy sequel; a definitive showcase for the genre's avenging heroine.

title: Truck Turner
shortDescription: 1974 action film starring composer Isaac Hayes
description: Jonathan Kaplan's 1974 AIP action film starring Isaac Hayes as a bounty hunter, with Hayes also providing the score.

title: Three the Hard Way
shortDescription: 1974 action film teaming three of the genre's stars
description: Gordon Parks Jr.'s 1974 action film uniting Jim Brown, Fred Williamson, and Jim Kelly against a white-supremacist plot; a marquee team-up of the era's leading men.

title: Dolemite
shortDescription: 1975 self-produced cult film by Rudy Ray Moore
description: D'Urville Martin's 1975 film starring Rudy Ray Moore as the kung-fu-fighting pimp Dolemite; a self-financed cult landmark celebrated in the 2019 film Dolemite Is My Name.

title: Shaft (soundtrack)
shortDescription: Isaac Hayes's 1971 Oscar- and Grammy-winning soundtrack album
description: Isaac Hayes's 1971 double-album soundtrack to Shaft; its Theme from Shaft won the Academy Award for Best Original Song and the album won two Grammys, a commercial landmark for the genre's music.

title: Super Fly (soundtrack)
shortDescription: Curtis Mayfield's 1972 landmark soundtrack album
description: Curtis Mayfield's 1972 soundtrack to Super Fly; a critically acclaimed, socially conscious album that topped the charts and is often ranked among the greatest soundtracks ever recorded.
